info.title: Fleetwright coordinator
info.summary: Long-running Claude Code sessions on machines you own, driven from a phone.
info.description:
There are TWO implementations of this API — a Cloudflare Worker with a Durable Object, and a Node process — and they are required to behave identically. This document is the contract between them, and `test/openapi.test.js` walks it and asserts both.

That is the reason it exists. It is not primarily documentation: five separate parity bugs reached this branch before it was written, the last of which (`GET /api/events` existing on one coordinator and not the other) was found in about ten seconds by listing both route tables side by side.

CONVENTIONS THAT ARE NOT OBVIOUS:

- Every response carries `ok`. A 200 with `ok: false` is normal and means the fleet answered and the answer was no.
- Errors carry `error.code` for a machine and `text` for a person. The text is written to be shown as-is; several of them are the only guidance an operator gets.
- A credential may arrive as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` OR as `?token=<token>`. The query form is deliberate: a Shortcut calls this through "Get Contents of URL" and cannot set headers. Both are read by one function so the two forms can never diverge — they did once, and `?token=fwk_` was full access.

servers.description: a Node coordinator on a box

tags.name: public
tags.description: Reachable with no credential, deliberately. Each one is here for a stated reason.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Becoming allowed in: signing in, enrolling a machine.

tags.name: fleet
tags.description: What exists and what it is doing.

bearer.description: A per-device credential (`fwk_<id>_<secret>`) issued by POST /api/session, or the break-glass admin token. Phones use the former; the latter can stop every session in the fleet.

queryToken.name: token
queryToken.description: The same credential, for callers that cannot set a header. Shortcuts, mostly.

name.description: Generated and stable, e.g. cc-brave-otter. The identity everything keys on.

title.description: What the work is. For people.

hostId.description: Which box. Attached by the coordinator on fan-out, because two hosts can hold the same name.

rcUrl.description: Remote Control, if this session has published one.

startedAt.description: When this run of it started, epoch ms on the host's clock. A timestamp rather than a duration, because a duration is stale the moment it is serialised and the client doing the arithmetic is the only place it stays right.

prompt.description: What it is asking, when the host recognised the question on its pane. Null when it is asking nothing, and also when it is waiting on something the host cannot read: `awaitingSince` says whether a person is needed, this says what for.

awaitingSince.description: Since when it has been blocked on a person, epoch ms on the host's clock, or null when it is not. The earlier of the session's own hook saying a dialog went up and the host's watcher first seeing one on the pane, so it is a lower bound on how long it has waited: the watcher looks every twenty seconds, and one that restarted begins counting again.

phases.description: How this run of the session has spent its time, from its own lifecycle hooks. Null is CANNOT TELL (not running, a session image older than the hooks, nothing reported yet in this run) and never zero. The totals are CLOSED time, up to `currentSince`; the client adds the open stretch from its own clock.

since.description: When the host started counting: the first hook of this run. Nothing before it is in any total.

awaitingMs.description: Blocked on a person: a dialog that needs an answer.

readyMs.description: At its own prompt, waiting for the next instruction.

spent.description: What the conversation has cost, as Claude Code counted it in the `cost-state` line it writes into its own transcript. Never estimated by the fleet: there is no price table here. Null is CANNOT TELL (no such line yet, a CLI that does not write one, a transcript the host cannot read).

usd.description: Claude Code's own figure, at API prices. On a Pro or Max sign-in that is not what anybody is billed.

complete.description: False unless Claude Code said every model it used had a known price; when false, `usd` is a floor.

asOf.description: When Claude Code wrote the figure, epoch ms. It writes one when a turn ends with nothing queued behind it, so a session in the middle of a turn is reported as of its last pause.

state.description: Four values, not three. `offline` is what a host becomes when its socket drops — a fact we know, distinct from `unknown`, which is what we say when we have not heard recently enough to be sure. A client that collapses them reports a box we KNOW is gone as a box we cannot see, which is the more alarming of the two and the less accurate.

reason.description: Why it is not healthy, as a sentence. The registry works hard to make "we don't know" unrepresentable.

fingerprint.description: 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over the public key. Compare against what the box prints.

event.description: session.awaiting-input, session.ended, session.error, session.rc-online, host.enrolled, host.refused, host.revoked, enrol.minted, intent

actor.description: The verified email of whoever asked. Null for events the fleet originated.

Prompt.description: What a session is asking, when the host recognised the shape of it. Never raw pane text — see src/fleet/host/prompt.js.

id.description: Names this question as rendered. An answer that no longer matches is refused rather than typed into whatever is on screen instead.

question.description: Written by the fleet, drawn from a fixed vocabulary. Never lifted from the terminal.

get.description: No host names, no counts. A liveness endpoint that leaks the fleet is not a liveness endpoint.

post.summary: Sign in, and receive a credential for this device
post.description: The one route that takes an identity token rather than a fleet credential, because it is where a fleet credential comes from. The ID token is verified against the provider's published keys and the address checked against the fleet's allowlist. Rate limited.

idToken.description: From Sign in with Apple or Google.

deviceName.description: Names the credential in the fleet's device list.

200.description: The only time the credential exists in full. The coordinator keeps a hash.

401.description: The token did not verify, and the reason says which check failed. `token_reused` means it already bought a credential: a token is exchanged once.

403.description: Verified, and not allowed in. `private_relay` means Hide My Email, which can never match a domain.

429.description: Too many attempts from this address.

503.description: This coordinator has no sign-in configured.

507.description: this fleet cannot store another credential

post.description: An invitation, not a way in — it requires a credential. A pin is short-lived, single-use and purpose-bound. Bind it to a host id to allow replacing that machine's key; an unbound pin may only ADD a machine.

hostId.description: Bind the pin to one machine.

readmit.description: Allow this pin to bring back a REVOKED host.

ephemeral.description: Admit a host that is expected to vanish: a disconnect retires the entry and revokes its key, and the scheduler will not place ordinary work on it. Decided here rather than claimed by the host — see docs/ephemeral-hosts.md.

install.description: The one line that installs a fresh box and joins it with this pin — `curl -fsSL <origin>/install | sudo FLEETWRIGHT_ENROL_PIN=123456 sh`. Null when this coordinator publishes no installer, or for a device pin; an older coordinator omits it. The pin rides as an environment variable, never in the URL.

get.description: Codes are masked. This answers "what did I leave lying around", not "what is the pin".

post.summary: Spend a pin to register a machine's public key
post.description: Reachable without a credential BECAUSE it is how a machine that has none gets one. The pin is the authorisation.

publicJwk.description: P-256 public key. A private key here is refused.

200.description: enrolled, re-enrolled or readmitted — `text` says which

400.description: the key or the host id was not acceptable

403.description: the pin was wrong, spent, expired, or minted for another host

507.description: this fleet is holding as many machines as it can store

post.description: Unauthenticated by necessity — asking for a nonce is what an unauthenticated party does in order to become authenticated. Nothing is stored: the nonce carries its own proof that this coordinator issued it, so a flood costs the coordinator nothing and cannot evict anybody else's.

post.summary: The same check /host/connect makes, without the socket
post.description: So `fleetwright-sidecar doctor` can tell an operator that the key on disk was never enrolled, or has been revoked, instead of leaving them to read a reconnect loop out of the journal.

401.description: and the reason distinguishes not-enrolled, revoked, expired, already-used and wrong-key

get.summary: Everything a client can see about the fleet

runners.description: Whether YOU can start a temporary machine here, and from where. Your own runner repository when you set one (`own: true`), the fleet’s otherwise, and null when neither exists — so a client offers `provision` only where it does something. Absent from an older coordinator, which means the same.

own.description: true when this is your own runner repository rather than the fleet’s. Absent from an older coordinator, which had only the fleet’s.

vmImages.description: The machine images YOU can start a VM from, on your own hypervisor: one per image, from the boxes holding a pool token you kept in your vault. Empty when no box holds one of yours. Start one with `provision` (platform `vm`, `template`). Absent from an older coordinator, which means the same.

template.description: the image’s id in Xen Orchestra, which `provision` takes as `template`

address.description: the Xen Orchestra it is on

hosts.description: the permanent boxes that can make it

networks.description: the pool’s networks the fleet may use, which `provision` takes as `network` instead of the uplink behind the edge router

groups.description: the pool's group networks, made by the hypervisor's policy: a machine joins one as well as its own network to reach the others in its group (`provision.group`)

labs.description: the pool's labs: networks of their own on its edge router, made by the hypervisor's policy. A machine in one (`provision` with platform `lab` and the lab's id as `network`) is on it alone and reaches the internet when the lab is open, or only the fleet and Claude when it is closed. Absent or empty: the pool has none, or the box holding it predates labs.

open.description: true: it reaches the internet; false: only the fleet and Claude

free.description: no machine is on it, by the box’s last look, and none was just asked for there

vmMachines.description: The machines already made from your images, as the boxes holding your pools last saw them: one per name. Work one with `vmctl`. Absent from an older coordinator, which means none can be shown.

madeAt.description: when it was made, epoch ms

net.description: what it sent and received as the hypervisor counted it; null is cannot tell (a box older than this, a pool that did not say, or a stopped machine)

end.description: the last point's time, epoch ms

rx.description: bytes a second, one point an interval, oldest first; null is a gap

tx.description: bytes a second, one point an interval, oldest first; null is a gap

group.description: the group network it is also on, by name

groupIp.description: its address on that group network

lab.description: the lab it is in, by its network’s name, and whether that lab is open; null is in no lab

address.description: the Xen Orchestra it is on

standby.description: kept ready and not yet taken by a session

vmStandby.description: What you keep ready on your hypervisor and how many are, or null when you keep none. Set with PUT /api/vm-standby.

since.description: when the oldest machine still being made was asked for, in epoch milliseconds; absent when none is

failed.description: why the last machine asked for did not come, kept until one does; absent when nothing has failed

get.summary: Which machines are in this fleet, with their key fingerprints
get.description: Carries no key material. The fingerprint is for a person to compare against what the box prints.

delete.summary: Remove a machine from the fleet
delete.description: Revoked AND disconnected: a revoked host holding a live socket is still in the fleet until something closes it. Marked rather than deleted, so a host that reconnects is told it was revoked rather than that it was never known.

404.description: no such host, or already revoked

get.summary: Who this credential belongs to, whether they are an admin, and which view this request is answered in
get.description: So an app draws admin-only controls for admins and nothing for members, instead of drawing them for everyone and refusing after the tap. `admin` is the same check the destructive routes make, and it grants nothing. Any request carrying `x-fleetwright-view: member` from an admin is answered as a member's would be (filtered lists, admin routes refused), so an admin can see what the people they invite see; `viewing` says which view this reply is in, and `admin` keeps the real role so the app can offer the way back. The header can only take privilege away.

get.summary: Which devices can reach this fleet
get.description: Without secrets — the coordinator stores a hash, not a token.

delete.summary: Revoke one device, leaving every other alone
delete.description: Which is the whole point of there being more than one credential.

404.description: no such client, or already revoked

get.description: The allow list an admin grew by hand, as opposed to the one in the deployment’s configuration. An invitation grants nothing by itself: it names WHICH ADDRESS may sign in.

403.description: not an admin — inviting is the admin seat’s

post.description: Adds the address to the allow list and, when the deployment can send mail, emails them the two store links. The reply says whether the email went, because “invited” and “told” are different facts.

note.description: a line for the email, in the inviter’s words

200.description: invited — `text` says whether an email was sent

403.description: not an admin — inviting is the admin seat’s

507.description: this fleet has as many invitations outstanding as it can store

delete.description: Removes the address from the allow list. A credential they already hold is a separate row and is revoked from /api/clients/{id}.

403.description: not an admin — inviting is the admin seat’s

get.summary: What happened while you were asleep
get.description: Push wakes a phone; this tells it what it missed. Capped at the same page size on both coordinators.

post.description: The fixed verb set is the security model: this API cannot express a shell string even to itself, so a compromised coordinator can start and stop sessions and can never run anything. A caller-supplied `actor` is a label; a signed-in device's verified email overrides it.

id.description: Idempotency key, honoured: a retried `start` returns the original outcome rather than a second session.

host.description: Placement preference for `start`: run the session on this host. Beside the intent rather than in params, because `start` declares no host parameter — a host receiving one would refuse the intent. Ignored for pinned and fan-out verbs. Refused by name if the host is unknown, degraded, or full.

start.description: For `provision` only: a session to start on the runner once it joins the fleet, as `start` would take it — `task`, `title`, `brief` and `mode`. Held by the coordinator with the dispatch ticket and started on the runner’s first health frame, as the person who asked. `task` is the words it starts working on; without one it comes up idle. No profile or secret: a runner holds neither.

200.description: The fleet answered. `ok: false` here means the answer was no.

post.description: Keyed by the push token rather than an id we mint, because the token is what identifies a delivery target — and a reinstall gives the same phone a new one, which should not accumulate as a second registration that fails forever.

403.description: that push token is registered to another device

507.description: this fleet is holding as many push registrations as it can store

post.summary: Send this device a notification now
post.description: Push fails silently by nature: a registration that never arrived and a provider that was never configured look identical from a phone, which is to say they look like nothing at all. This is the only way to find out before the notification that matters.

200.description: sent, or a reason it was not

post.description:
Apple POSTs a signed JWT here when a user changes mail forwarding, REVOKES this app from their Apple ID settings, or deletes their Apple Account. The last two mean a person has withdrawn consent, and every credential issued to that address is revoked — along with the push registrations that went with them.

Public by necessity: Apple holds no credential of ours, so the signature on the JWT is the entire authentication. Anyone may POST here; only a message signed by Apple, for this app's audience, does anything.

Answers 200 to anything it can verify, including notifications it deliberately ignores, because Apple retries on failure and there is nothing to gain from making it retry a message we understood.

200.description: verified — acted on, or deliberately ignored

503.description: this coordinator has no audience configured, so it cannot check one

get.description: Where GitHub redirects a browser after somebody authorizes the App. Unauthenticated by necessity — a browser carries no fleet credential — and secured by `state`: unguessable, single-use, minutes-long, and bound to the host and person who started the flow. Returns HTML, because the thing reading it is a browser. Absent a configured App, every request here is refused.

200.description: Connected. An HTML page telling the person they can close the tab.

400.description: Refused — unknown, expired or already-used state, or GitHub declined.

get.summary: Finish a GitHub sign-in made through the OAuth relay
get.description: Where the OAuth relay (docs/relay-terms.md) sends a browser back, for a coordinator that has the App's client id and not its secret. The relay exchanged the code and sealed the token to this coordinator's registered key; only this coordinator can open it. Unauthenticated by necessity and secured like the callback: the `state` is single-use and minted here, and the same state must be found again inside what was sealed. Returns HTML. A coordinator with no relay configured refuses every request here.

parameters.name: sealed
parameters.description: The token, sealed to this coordinator's key. Absent when `error` is present.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: What went wrong at the relay, in one word.

200.description: Connected. An HTML page telling the person they can close the tab.

400.description: Refused: unknown, expired or already-used state, a sealed token that does not open or was made for another state, or what the relay said went wrong.

get.description: Where Cloudflare redirects a browser after somebody authorizes this fleet's OAuth client. The same shape as the GitHub callback and secured the same way: unauthenticated by necessity — a browser carries no fleet credential — with a `state` that is unguessable, single-use, minutes-long, and bound to the host and person who started the flow. Returns HTML, because the thing reading it is a browser. Absent a configured client, every request here is refused.

200.description: Connected. An HTML page telling the person they can close the tab.

400.description: Refused — unknown, expired or already-used state, or Cloudflare declined.

get.description: Every token for an admin; only their own for a member. A runner token is how a repository’s workflow enrols an ephemeral host as the person who minted it — see docs/ephemeral-hosts.md.

post.description: Belongs to the signed-in person, so runs it enrols are attributed to them. The admin token cannot mint one: a runner has to be somebody’s.

name.description: what it is for, usually the repository

403.description: not signed in as a person

507.description: this fleet cannot store another runner token

delete.description: Runs still using it are refused at enrolment from then on. A member can revoke their own; an admin any.

404.description: no such token, or not yours — the two are not distinguished on purpose

get.summary: Your linked repositories, one per role
get.description: One list with a role on each link, because the three roles want different visibility, credentials and warnings: `links` holds `{ role, repo, setAt }` for each role you have linked, and `fleet.runners` is the fleet’s runner repository, which is what you get without one of your own. See docs/linked-repos.md.

403.description: not signed in as a person

put.summary: Link a repository for one role, once it passes that role’s check
put.description: Checked as the Fleetwright GitHub App by the minting Worker, or on a permanent box with YOUR GitHub connection (`linkrepo`): an `archive` has to be private and writable, `runners` public with the runner workflows and Actions write, `templates` either and readable. Saved, as GitHub spells it, only if it passes; the check comes back either way, as `linkedRepo`. Linking an archive means the sessions you start from then on are pushed to it, each on a branch of its own, before they stop.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: `archive` (private: where your sessions are pushed before they stop), `runners` (public: where your temporary machines start, the runner repository by another route) or `templates` (either: skills, presets, configs and workflows a session may read)

400.description: not a role, or not an owner/repo

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: the check did not pass, so nothing was linked: `linkedRepo` says which answer, `text` what to fix, and `needsConnection` when no box holds your GitHub connection

delete.summary: Unlink the repository for one role
delete.description: Sessions you start afterwards are not pushed to an archive; ones already running keep the archive they started with. Unlinking `runners` is clearing your runner repository.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: `archive` (private: where your sessions are pushed before they stop), `runners` (public: where your temporary machines start, the runner repository by another route) or `templates` (either: skills, presets, configs and workflows a session may read)

200.description: unlinked, or there was nothing to unlink

403.description: not signed in as a person

get.description: Where your temporary machines come from: `repo` is yours, null when you have not set one, and `fleet` is the fleet’s, which is what you get without one. See docs/runner-central.md.

403.description: not signed in as a person

put.summary: Set your runner repository, once it passes the check
put.description: A permanent box checks it with YOUR GitHub connection — public, the Fleetwright GitHub App installed with Actions write, and which runner workflows it carries — and it is saved, as GitHub spells it, only if every answer is one a dispatch can use. The check comes back either way, as `runnerRepo`.

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: the check did not pass, so nothing was saved: `runnerRepo` says which answer, `text` what to fix, and `needsConnection` when no box holds your GitHub connection

delete.description: Your machines come from the fleet’s repository again, when it has one.

200.description: cleared, or there was nothing to clear

403.description: not signed in as a person

get.summary: Machines you keep ready on your hypervisor
get.description: What you keep ready and how many are: `vmStandby` is `{ template, count, network, ready, starting }`, or null when you keep none. See docs/hypervisors.md, “Machines kept ready”.

403.description: not signed in as a person

put.description: Keep `count` machines (0 to 3) from `template` booted and joined, on `network` or behind the edge router, so a session on that image starts on one at once. 0 keeps none; machines kept beyond the new count are ended.

template.description: a machine image, as `vmImages` lists it

network.description: a network of the pool, as the image lists it; null is behind the edge router

400.description: a count, image or network that is not one

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: no box offers that image now, or the fleet keeps as many as it can store

post.summary: Start a runner from your own device
post.description: Mints the dispatch ticket `provision` would, and holds the session to start when the runner joins, but hands the dispatch to the caller instead of to a permanent box: `repo`, `workflow` and `inputs` are what to send GitHub's `POST /repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow}/dispatches` with the caller's own GitHub sign-in, on the repository's default branch. No permanent box is involved. See docs/runner-central.md.

start.description: a session to start when it joins: `task`, `title`, `brief`, `mode`, as `start` takes them

400.description: not a platform, or minutes out of range

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: nowhere to start one: no runner repository is set for you or for the fleet

get.summary: Start signing in to GitHub on this device
get.description: The App's client id and the callback GitHub sends the browser back through, for a device that runs GitHub's sign-in page itself with its own PKCE verifier and a state beginning `d.`. Not the client secret: that stays in the minting Worker, which finishes the exchange (POST). The callback hands the code back to the app at `fleetwright://github` and exchanges nothing.

403.description: not signed in as a person

503.description: this fleet has no GitHub App configured

post.summary: Finish or renew this device's GitHub sign-in
post.description: `sealed` is `{ v: 1, grant: 'code'|'refresh', code, verifier, redirectUri, refreshToken, reply, at }` sealed on the device to the minting Worker's deposit key. The coordinator relays it unread; the minter makes the exchange with the client secret only it holds, and returns the token sealed to `reply`, a key only the device has. See docs/runner-central.md.

200.description: `sealed`, the token for the device, and `text`

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: refused: `error.code` and `text` say why (stale, sealed to another key, GitHub refused the code, no minter)

get.summary: The key your Claude login is sealed to
get.description: The minting Worker's deposit key, as it states it. The deposit tool compares it with the pin your operator gave you and refuses when they differ, because a coordinator is exactly what would swap it. See docs/runner-central.md, “Your Claude login on a runner”.

403.description: not signed in as a person

503.description: this fleet's minting Worker keeps no Claude logins

put.summary: Deposit, replace or forget your Claude login
put.description: `sealed` is a `claude setup-token` and a GitHub token of yours, sealed on your computer to the minting Worker's key, so this coordinator carries it unread. The minter asks GitHub whose account the GitHub token is, keeps the Claude token for that account's runners, and discards the GitHub token. A null Claude token forgets the one kept.

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: refused by the minter: `error.code` and `text` say why — stale, sealed to another key, not a token, or GitHub would not say whose

post.summary: Admit a GitHub Actions job as an ephemeral host
post.description: Reachable without a credential BECAUSE the job’s OIDC token is the credential: verified against GitHub’s keys, bound to the repositories in FLEETWRIGHT_ACTIONS_REPOS, and single-use. Returns a pin the runner spends at /api/enroll/host — see docs/ephemeral-hosts.md.

ticket.description: a single-use ticket from a `provision` dispatch, which attributes the run to the person who asked for it

403.description: the token did not verify, or names a repository this fleet does not admit — `error.code` is `bad_token`

503.description: FLEETWRIGHT_ACTIONS_REPOS is unset — this coordinator admits no runners

post.summary: Admit a machine from your hypervisor as an ephemeral host
post.description: Reachable without a credential BECAUSE the ticket is the credential: minted by a `provision` for platform `vm`, single-use, forty-five minutes old at most, and bound to the person who asked. The box that cloned the machine booted it with the ticket in its cloud-init drive, which Xen Orchestra destroys after boot. The host id is derived from the ticket (`vm-<id>`), never chosen. See docs/hypervisors.md.

ticket.description: the `fwt_` ticket the machine was booted with

publicJwk.description: the machine’s own P-256 public key, made on it

400.description: the key is not a P-256 public key

403.description: not a machine ticket, spent, or expired — `error.code` is `unclaimed`

507.description: the fleet has no room for another host — `hosts_full`

post.description: `sealed` is `{ v: 1, github, email, op, at, reply, ... }` sealed on the device to the minting Worker's deposit key, where `op` is `list`, `put` or `forget` (a named secret `secret:NAME`, a hypervisor’s token record `hypervisor:ADDRESS`, or `claude`), `connect` (a GitHub or Cloudflare sign-in: `provider`, `code`, `verifier`, `redirectUri`), `grant` (`hostKey`, the box's public key, and `label`) or `revoke` (`key`). The coordinator relays it unread beside the signed-in account, which the minter checks against `email` inside the seal. The answer is sealed to `reply`. See docs/vault.md.

200.description: `sealed`, the answer for the device, and `text`

403.description: not signed in as a person

422.description: the minting Worker refused it, with a code and a sentence

get.summary: Start signing in to Cloudflare for your vault
get.description: The Cloudflare client id, the scopes this fleet asks for, the authorize page and the callback, for a device that runs Cloudflare's sign-in itself with its own PKCE verifier and a state beginning `d.`. The callback hands the code back to the app at `fleetwright://cloudflare`; the minting Worker makes the exchange through POST /api/vault. Not the client secret.

403.description: not signed in as a person

503.description: this fleet has no Cloudflare sign-in configured

post.summary: Register a Live Activity for a hypervisor setup
post.description: The phone that began an `xosetup` job posts the push token of the Live Activity it started, so progress reaches the Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island while the app is closed. Only the job's owner. Answers with where the job has got to.

400.description: Not a job id and a token.

403.description: Not signed in.

422.description: No such job for this person.

post.summary: A machine image's build VM reports a step of its install
post.description: Reachable without a credential BECAUSE the token is the credential: the box running a policy job asks the coordinator for it over its own socket (`image-reporter`, answered by `minted`), one live token per job, held as a hash, gone when the job ends or after an hour, good for 24 reports. The box writes it into the build VM's cloud-init drive, which the build deletes before the VM becomes the template. The step is passed to that box, whose sentence for it is what the phone shows. See docs/hypervisors.md.

token.description: the `fwi_` token the build VM was booted with

detail.description: with `failed` only: the end of the install log, cut to 2000 characters

202.description: passed to the machine running the build

400.description: not a step this build reports — `bad_step`

403.description: not a token this fleet gave a build, or the build is over — `unknown`

429.description: this token has carried all the reports it may — `too_many`

get.summary: Carry a relay through this phone, for a pool no machine reaches
get.description: A WebSocket. When no machine in the fleet reaches a Xen Orchestra address (the `xoprobe` answer names a machine in `relay`), the phone that is adding it opens this, and the coordinator joins it to frames to that one machine. The machine opens TLS over it itself and holds it to the pin, so the phone and the coordinator carry ciphertext; the phone connects to `address` on its own network and nowhere else. The first message is `{op: "ready", relay, hostId, address, expiresAt, maxBytes}`; then `open`, `data` (base64) and `end` for each connection the machine makes, and `closed` with a sentence when it ends. The phone answers `opened` or `refused`, then `data` and `end`. Name the relay in `xoprobe` and `xosetup begin` as `relay`. An admin's device credential only, and only that device may name the relay. One probe, then one job; fifteen minutes and 64 MiB at most; closed when the job ends. See docs/hypervisors.md, "Through the phone".

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Where Xen Orchestra answers, as the person typed it: a host name or address, with an optional port.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The machine to carry it for, as `xoprobe` named it in `relay.hostId`. Absent, the coordinator chooses.

101.description: The relay is open; the first message says which it is, or why it was closed.

403.description: Not a signed-in person’s device.
